newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Jan 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Jan 17.

text.p: The government intends to lift the state house rent freeze, boost the accommodation supplement and return to market rentals in March. The National-NZ First coalition placed an interim freeze on Housing NZ rents before Christmas "pending a review of affordability issues". Housing Minister Murray McCully said on Thursday the rent freeze had been set "for a sufficient period of time for the government to review the adequacy of the income support measures -- the accommodation supplement -- and adjust it". Page 1.

Prices for crossbred wools, New Zealand's main wool variety, slumped again at the year's second sale yesterday, prompting the Wool Board to warn farmers to spread their risk for the rest of the selling season. Page 1.

Power companies say they will smarten up their act after accusations in a Consumer Affairs Ministry report of high-handed attitudes and customer exploitation. The report says that, since deregulation in 1993, the companies have exploited their position as monopoly suppliers in a variety of ways. These include companies requiring customers to pay for meter faults, power they have not used, and problems caused by the power company. Page 2.

Immigration Minister Max Bradford has promised to review policy with a view to tightening up on foreign students' entitlement to student allowances. This follows an Education Ministry decision to take on a second fulltime staff member to investigate student fraud complaints. Of a total of 900 complaints of suspected abuse and fraud of student loans and allowances over the past two years, 200 have involved recent migrant residents. Page 2.

The Education Ministry underestimated the cost of school buildings by 50 percent, a management audit of the ministry says. This "major failure" occurred in the 1995 budget estimate of the cost of building schools and classrooms to cope with rolls growth during the next three years. Page 3.

December-quarter consumer price index data -- due today -- is expected to receive a muted reaction from the financial markets. Most economists are predicting underlying inflation to come in between 0.4 percent and 0.5 percent for the December quarter and either 2.1 percent or 2.2 percent for the year to December. Those expectations are in line or just below those forecast by the Reserve Bank, whic predicted both underlying and headline inflation to come in at 0.5 percent for the quarter and 2.3 percent for the year to December. Page 12.

Spectrum Resources said on Thursday the nickel resource at its 70 percent-owned mining project in Vietnam would probably be increased as the result of recent testing. The listed minerals company said in a statement to the stock exchange that a drilling programme at the Ban Phuc nickel project had been completed successfully. Page 12.

The Manufacturers Federation cautioned yesterday against increased government spending and short-term stimulation of the economy. Increased government spending, particularly in 1998-99 and the following year, would fuel the areas causing current inflation, chief executive Simon Arnold said. Unless the government found compensatory savings from its spending programme, or householders increased their savings, taking pressure off the local economy, exporters would continue to face an over-valued exchange rate, he said. Page 12.
